title: Data centres sustain US copper demand amid tariff decision wait
gist: Delegates at the American Copper Council Fall Meeting (Miami, 10–13 Nov) reported that the US data centre build-out is keeping copper demand hot, with wire, cable and tube makers citing record orders, even as the market awaits Washington's refined copper tariff decision. Because copper is only 0.5–1% of data centre capex, developers are price-insensitive and over-order to secure supply.

insights.claim: US wire and cable producers and tube manufacturers reported record orders at the American Copper Council Fall Meeting in November 2026, driven by the US data centre build-out.
insights.speaker: Michael Finch, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Semi-fabricator order books are a leading read on US copper demand; record orders point to sustained physical tightness tied to AI/data centre capex.
insights.locator: Wire and cable producers and tube

insights.claim: Copper accounts for only about 0.5–1% of data centre capex, so developers are insensitive to elevated copper prices and order freely to secure enough material.
insights.speaker: Michael Finch, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: Price-inelastic demand from data centres means high copper prices may not destroy demand in this segment; watch data centre capex as a copper demand driver.
insights.quote: Copper makes up only 0.5–1% of data centre capex
insights.locator: Wire and cable producers and tube

insights.claim: Data centre developers prioritise on-time delivery over material efficiency, accepting leftover copper cable on reels after construction, which inflates effective copper consumption.
insights.speaker: one US wire and cable producer (via Benchmark)
insights.so_what: Over-ordering and wastage add a buffer layer of demand that could reverse if build-out slows, creating destocking risk.
insights.quote: “They just don’t care how much is left on reels after construction has finished, what they care about is delivering on time,”

insights.claim: The US copper market is awaiting a Washington decision on refined copper tariffs, yet data centre demand has kept US copper demand running hot despite that uncertainty.
insights.speaker: Michael Finch, Benjamin Roche
insights.so_what: A tariff decision on refined copper is a key pending catalyst for US premiums (e.g., COMEX vs LME spread) and import flows.
insights.locator: The race to build data centres
